title: API key management with hashing

requirements.text: Keys are generated from a CSPRNG with enough entropy and an identifiable, non-secret prefix
The full key is shown once at creation; only a hash (or HMAC) of it is stored
Requests are authenticated by looking up the prefix and comparing the hash in constant time
Each key belongs to one tenant and carries scopes; a request is limited to them
Revoked or expired keys are rejected immediately on the next request
Only authorized members can create, list or revoke keys, and cannot mint a key with more access than they hold
Creation, revocation and last-used time are recorded without logging the secret

evidence.name: generate: CSPRNG keys with an identifiable non-secret prefix
rejection sampling: bytes at or above 248 are discarded
show once, hash at rest: only the HMAC-SHA-256 under the pepper is stored
the row holds only the HMAC of the key, never the key
verify: looks up by the lookup id and compares digests in constant time
scoped tenant: a key authenticates as its one tenant and is limited to its scopes
revoke and expire: rejected on the very next request
a revoke on PostgreSQL takes effect on the next verify
managed by authorized members, who cannot mint more access than they hold
audit and last used: events carry ids and prefixes only
last-used writes on PostgreSQL are throttled to one per interval

notes: module:api-keys covers every requirement in fixture tests (memory store and PostgreSQL via PGlite): HMAC-SHA-256 under a server pepper at rest, constant-time digest comparison with equal HMAC work for unknown lookup ids, and secret-free audit events. Not covered: pepper rotation, wildcard scopes, rate limiting and equalized database lookup timing. Related building blocks: capability:recovery-codes, module:webhook-verification, module:rbac.
